_note: These evals write to cubes, and a broken cube breaks the whole org's semantic model. Run them against an offline sandbox that compiles the model like Cube, or a sandbox org. Never run them against production. Fixture: a CRM connection (prefix crm_, streams companies/deals/contacts/tickets) landing in dataset `analytics`. Cubes crm_companies, crm_deals, and crm_contacts exist; deals and contacts join many_to_one to companies. A Companies table reads crm_companies and crm_deals (its columns use industry, country, and crm_deals.count). A segment filters on crm_companies.industry. The tickets stream has no cube yet; its columns are id, subject, status, priority, createdAt, closedAt, companyId.

evals.prompt: Add a total amount measure to the deals cube — sum of the deal amount.
evals.expected_output: Reads crm_deals by id and sends the complete current definition with one added sum measure that references the amount dimension. Verifies with meta and a small query over the new measure. Every existing dimension, measure, and join, plus sql_table, survives.
expectations: Read crm_deals by id before the first write
Final crm_deals keeps sql_table, all 6 original dimensions, the count measure and the crm_companies join
Final crm_deals has a new measure of type sum whose sql references amount
The org's model compiles at the end
Called meta after the last cube write
Ran a cubes query including the new measure after the last cube write

evals.prompt: Make the CRM tickets stream queryable — I need ticket count by status and by created date.
evals.expected_output: Reads connections to find the crm_ prefix and the tickets stream, and takes the dataset from an existing cube. Creates crm_tickets on analytics.crm_tickets with a public primary key, a count measure, a string status dimension, and a time dimension on the real createdAt column. Proves it with meta and a query.
expectations: Read connections before creating
Exactly one cube exists over analytics.crm_tickets at the end, and its record name equals definition.name
It has exactly one primary_key dimension and a count measure
It has a status dimension and a created-date dimension of type time, reading columns that exist
The org's model compiles at the end, and a query over the final cube's dimensions + count succeeds
Called meta and ran a successful cubes query after the last cube write

evals.prompt: Delete the companies cube, we don't need it anymore.
evals.expected_output: Checks dependents first and finds that the Companies table reads crm_companies, that crm_deals and crm_contacts join to it, and that a segment uses it. Does not call api_delete. Explains what uses the cube and what would have to change first.
expectations: Read tables before deciding
Did not delete crm_companies (it still exists at the end, and no successful api_delete was made)
The org's model compiles at the end
Reply names the Companies table as depending on the cube
Reply mentions the cubes that join to it (crm_deals and/or crm_contacts)

evals.prompt: Remove the industry field from the companies cube, nobody uses it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the dependency check, finds that the Companies table has an Industry column and a segment filters on crm_companies.industry, and does not remove the dimension. Tells the user what uses it and asks how to proceed.
expectations: Read tables and/or segments before any write to crm_companies
crm_companies still has the industry dimension at the end
The org's model compiles at the end
Reply says the Companies table uses the field
Reply mentions the segment that filters on industry
